chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The remarriage (raj'ah) is [valid] in the context of sexual intercourse; otherwise, it is only one [single] [revocation]."

key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةُ: Raj'ah, the act of a husband taking back his wife during the waiting period after a revocable divorce.
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One, referring to a single count of the revocation.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on counting revocations in a revocable divorce if the husband does not have sexual intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the mechanism of *raj'ah* (revocable divorce), establishing that sexual intercourse during the *iddah* period constitutes a complete, independent revocation, while non-coital acts do not. This distinction is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining whether a husband has exhausted his quota of three revocations, thereby transitioning the marriage to an irrevocable state (*ba'in*).
